$comment: One shard of the signal-lens catalogue. DATA, never loaded whole into an agent context. Validate with: python3 scripts/validate_catalogue.py

signals.name: Search query
signals.definition: The subject issues a query whose terms name the category, a product, a competitor, or the problem the product solves - either into the company's own site search, or into an external search engine that then delivers the click. Qualifying condition: a query string is captured and attributed to a session, and the string matches a maintained category, brand, competitor or problem lexicon.
signals.question_answered: Is this person actively looking for what we sell, and in whose words - the category's, ours, or a competitor's?

capability_ladder.how: Log the query string your own site-search box already receives, with a session identifier and timestamp, and bucket it against a hand-written category / brand / competitor / problem lexicon
capability_ladder.gives: The highest-intent free text you will ever own, in the same week, with no third party in the path

capability_ladder.how: Pull query-to-landing-page data for your own verified domain from the search engine's webmaster console and join it to the page it landed on
capability_ladder.gives: The external demand vocabulary, but aggregated to page and day, with rare queries withheld - never a person

capability_ladder.how: Preserve the paid-search keyword and click identifier on the landing URL and persist them onto the session record
requires: landing pages and redirects that do not strip query parameters
capability_ladder.gives: Query-level intent joined to a real session, for the slice of demand you pay for

min_data.note: Below roughly 200 queries in a lexicon bucket per month the bucket rate is noise. Read the individual queries instead - at low volume they are more informative than any score computed from them.

access_conditions: Webmaster-console query data is aggregated and rare queries are withheld to protect the person who typed them, so rung 2 is vocabulary, never a subject-level signal

Query text is free text and will occasionally contain special-category terms; matching it to a commercial lexicon is in scope, deriving a health, life-event or household attribute from it is not, and that class is documented as a prohibition with no implementation path
Paid click identifiers are supplied under the ad platform's terms, which restrict redistribution and re-identification
signals.terms_note: Webmaster-console and paid-search query data arrive under platform API terms that limit redistribution and prohibit attempts to re-identify the searcher.

freshness.note: A query states what the person wanted at that moment. It stops describing them within days unless it repeats.

false_positives: Competitor or price-scraper reconnaissance running your catalogue through your own search box
Job applicants searching for careers, benefits or office locations
Existing customers searching for support articles, invoices or documentation
Student or academic research
Employees testing search relevance from inside the business
Bots and LLM agents issuing scripted queries with no human behind them
Navigational queries from people who wanted a different brand entirely

evidence.note: Verified this session: rare queries are omitted from the report table to protect user privacy, which is why console query data cannot be resolved to a person.

signals.name: Website browsing depth
signals.definition: The subject views a set of pages whose classification marks them as commercial research rather than support, careers or press - product, category, solution, use-case or documentation pages - with enough depth or repetition to separate the visit from a bounce. Qualifying condition: two or more commercially classified pageviews inside one session, or a return visit to the same commercial page cluster.
signals.question_answered: Is anyone actually researching us, or are we counting arrivals - and which part of the offer are they working through?

capability_ladder.how: Write a lookup table from URL pattern to page class (commercial, support, careers, press, legal) and score the pageview stream you already collect against it
capability_ladder.gives: Separates research from traffic using data already on disk - the table is an afternoon's work and it is the whole signal

capability_ladder.how: Add engagement events - scroll depth and active time rather than time-on-page - so a page that was read is distinguished from a page that was loaded
capability_ladder.gives: Removes the largest source of noise: open tabs and single-scroll bounces scored as study

capability_ladder.how: Stitch sessions to a persistent same-origin first-party identifier so browsing depth accumulates across weeks instead of resetting every visit
requires: a server-set identifier on your own origin
capability_ladder.gives: Depth measured over a consideration cycle rather than a single sitting

min_data.note: Page-class depth rates are unstable below roughly 100 sessions per class per week; under that, use browsing as a per-subject flag rather than a rate to compare against.

access_conditions: Page classification is the signal. Without it, a careers page and a pricing page carry identical weight and the depth measure is meaningless
Bot and agent traffic must be filtered before depth is computed, not after, or the deepest sessions in the dataset will belong to crawlers

freshness.note: Browsing depth describes an open research window; it stops predicting once the window closes with either a purchase or silence.

false_positives: Crawlers, uptime monitors and LLM agents fetching pages at machine depth
Competitor research reading the full positioning stack
Job applicants working through the site before an interview
Analysts, press and students profiling the company
Existing customers using marketing pages as documentation
Employees and agency staff browsing their own site
A left-open tab producing dwell that was never attention

signals.name: Channel switching
signals.definition: The same subject appears in a second channel shortly after acting in a first - opens an email then lands on the site, moves from the site to live chat, a call or a booked appointment, from app to web, or from online to a store or showroom. Qualifying condition: two channel-attributed events resolve to one subject identifier inside a stated window, and the second channel costs the subject more effort than the first.
signals.question_answered: Has this person escalated from channels that cost them nothing to channels that cost them effort - and where do they want to transact?

capability_ladder.how: Carry your own subject identifier on every outbound link you send - email, SMS, printed code - and write it onto the session on arrival, so the message-to-web switch joins with no new system
requires: control of your own outbound link templates
capability_ladder.gives: The most common switch, closed this week, using systems you already pay for

capability_ladder.how: Stamp the same identifier into chat, callback, quote and appointment forms so web-to-assisted switches land in the same table as the web events
requires: form and chat widgets that accept a hidden field
capability_ladder.gives: The escalation that matters most - anonymous browsing becoming a request for a human

capability_ladder.how: Join the store, branch or contact-centre record on an identifier the subject already gives you there - loyalty number, phone, order reference - to close the online-to-offline switch
requires: a shared identifier collected in both places
capability_ladder.gives: The switch that is invisible to every web analytics tool, and the one physical retailers are judged on

min_data.note: State the join window explicitly and hold it constant. A window wide enough to catch every switch will also join two unrelated people who share an inbox or a phone.

access_conditions: The join needs one identifier the subject supplies in both channels; without it, cross-channel matching becomes probabilistic and the signal stops being evidence
Contact-centre and store records are usually held under a different lawful basis and retention schedule than web events; joining them does not merge those obligations

freshness.note: A switch into an assisted channel is a request for a response now; its value collapses over days, not weeks.

false_positives: Existing customers escalating a billing or delivery problem, which reads as purchase intent and is not
A switch caused by failure rather than interest - a broken page, a form that would not submit, a search that returned nothing
A forwarded email or shared inbox, so the person in the second channel is not the person in the first
Assistants, agencies and proxy researchers acting on someone else's behalf
Job applicants moving from a careers page into chat
A single person using two devices being counted as a switch rather than a continuation

signals.name: Device and session continuity
signals.definition: The same subject returns across separate sessions or surfaces - a second visit days later, a phone session followed by a desktop session - where the return is established by an identifier the subject supplied or by a same-origin identifier your own server set, and not by probabilistic matching. Qualifying condition: two or more sessions resolve to one subject over a stated horizon, with the basis of that resolution recorded alongside it.
signals.question_answered: Are we looking at one researcher whose consideration is building over weeks, or at a stream of unrelated first visits that our counters are inflating?

capability_ladder.how: Set the visitor identifier from your own server on your own origin rather than from a script, and count sessions per identifier
requires: the ability to set a cookie in an HTTP response from your own domain
capability_ladder.gives: A return horizon measured in months instead of the seven days that script-written storage gets on privacy-restricting browsers

capability_ladder.how: Promote the identifier to a durable subject id at any moment the subject declares themselves - login, newsletter, saved basket, quote form - and backfill the prior sessions onto it
capability_ladder.gives: Continuity that survives storage clearing, because it is anchored to something the person gave you

capability_ladder.how: Join the surfaces the person has authenticated on - web, mobile app, email - on that same declared identifier so continuity is deterministic across devices
requires: authentication on more than one surface
capability_ladder.gives: Cross-device continuity with a basis you can show the person, and no third party in the graph

min_data.note: State the horizon before measuring. Return rates computed over an unstated horizon are not comparable to anything, including your own previous number.

access_conditions: A CNAME-delegated subdomain served by a third-party script is not the same as a same-origin server-set identifier; privacy-restricting browsers cap cookies set in responses to CNAME-cloaked requests to seven days, so a managed 'first-party' identifier of that kind does not buy the long horizon it is sold as buying

Probabilistic cross-device and shared-network linkage is deliberately absent from this ladder. Binding devices together because they share a network resolves a household without anyone having declared anything, which is household-composition inference rather than a continuity measure, and belongs with the prohibited classes that carry no implementation path
Every stored return count must carry its resolution basis, because a count built on a seven-day identifier and a count built on a login mean different things and cannot be pooled

freshness.note: A return pattern describes an open consideration window. Once returns stop, the accumulated count keeps overstating the subject unless it decays.

false_positives: A shared household, office or shop-floor device carrying one identifier for several people
One person clearing storage or using private browsing, appearing as many first-time visitors
Persistent bots and monitoring agents that accept and return cookies
Existing customers whose returns are support-driven rather than purchase-driven
Corporate networks and VPNs concentrating unrelated people behind one egress path
An assistant or agent session returning on behalf of the person who will actually decide

evidence.note: Verified this session: 'ITP now detects third-party CNAME cloaking requests and caps the expiry of any cookies set in the HTTP response to 7 days.' Published by the browser engine's own maintainers about their own product.
Verified this session: script-writable storage is deleted after seven days of browser use without user interaction on the site, which is the cap rung 1 exists to escape.

signals.name: Advertising response
signals.definition: The subject responds to a paid placement - clicks a search, social, retail-media or display ad, or completes an action inside the ad unit - and the click identifier survives to the landing session, so the response is attributable to a specific placement rather than to a channel in aggregate. Qualifying condition: a session carries a click or campaign identifier that resolves to a known placement, and that session contains at least one post-click event.
signals.question_answered: Which paid message is pulling people who then behave like buyers, as opposed to which one buys the cheapest clicks?

capability_ladder.how: Preserve the click identifier and campaign parameters through every redirect, consent wall and login bounce, and write them onto the first-party session record on arrival
requires: landing pages and redirects that do not strip query parameters
capability_ladder.gives: Placement-level response using identifiers the platform already appends for free - no contract, no new vendor

capability_ladder.how: Report your own post-click outcomes back to the platform from your server, keyed on the stored click identifier, instead of relying on a browser tag firing
requires: an outcome definition you actually believe in
capability_ladder.gives: Response measured against your outcomes rather than the platform's view of them, and it survives blocked tags

capability_ladder.how: Reconcile platform-reported clicks against landing sessions on a daily export and publish the gap as a standing number
capability_ladder.gives: An honest measure of how much of your paid traffic is unobservable, which is the number every downstream ratio depends on

min_data.note: Below roughly 100 clicks a placement's post-click rate is noise; roll up to campaign or audience before comparing anything.

access_conditions: Click identifiers are supplied under the ad platform's terms; those terms restrict redistribution and prohibit using the identifier to re-identify the person outside the platform's own measurement
A large share of paid clicks arrive with parameters stripped by in-app browsers, redirect chains and privacy settings; the gap is a property of the channel, not a bug to be engineered away
signals.terms_note: Ad platform terms govern the use of click identifiers and of any outcome data sent back; several jurisdictions treat outbound conversion reporting as a sharing of personal data requiring an opt-out path.

freshness.note: An ad click is the weakest act in this family and the fastest to stop meaning anything; it is useful mainly as the opening of a session, not as a standing fact about a person.

false_positives: Accidental taps, which are a large and well-known share of mobile display clicks
Click fraud and bot traffic bought alongside real inventory
Competitors clicking to inspect landing pages or to spend your budget
Existing customers clicking brand ads they would have reached organically
Response to a discount or a giveaway rather than to the product
Ad-verification and brand-safety crawlers following creative links
Curiosity clicks on a creative that misrepresented the destination

signals.name: Offline QR or code response
signals.definition: The subject scans a code printed or broadcast on a physical surface - packaging, a shelf label, a poster, a receipt, a vehicle, an event badge, a screen - or types a code shown offline, and lands on a URL whose parameters identify that specific placement. Qualifying condition: a session arrives on a URL carrying a placement identifier that exists only on an offline surface.
signals.question_answered: Which physical placements are producing real digital sessions - and is this person standing in front of the product right now?

capability_ladder.how: Give every printed surface its own code or URL parameter and keep one table mapping code to placement; log the parameter on arrival
requires: the ability to print or label distinct codes
capability_ladder.gives: Placement-level attribution for the cost of a spreadsheet and a redirect - the cheapest offline-to-digital measurement that exists

capability_ladder.how: Route every code through a redirect service on your own domain so the scan is counted before the landing page renders, and so a printed code can be repointed after it has shipped
capability_ladder.gives: Scan counts that survive a broken landing page, and printed assets that stay useful after a campaign ends

capability_ladder.how: Join the placement identifier to the store, shelf, route or event record so a scan arrives carrying its physical context
requires: a placement register maintained by whoever installs the surfaces
capability_ladder.gives: In-aisle and in-venue intent - a scan that says where the person is, not only that they scanned

min_data.note: One code per placement is the real minimum, and it is unrecoverable: a code reused across placements can never be separated afterwards, no matter how many scans it collects.

access_conditions: Coarse location, where it is captured at all, comes from the landing session and not from the scan; the code itself carries the placement, which is the more reliable of the two and needs no device permission
Codes on packaging outlive the campaign that printed them; a redirect you control is the only way to retire a destination without recalling the product

freshness.note: A scan means the person was physically present at that surface. Within days that fact is history rather than context.

false_positives: Curiosity scans by passers-by, children and people testing whether the code works
Staff and installers verifying placements after a print run
Link-preview fetchers in messaging apps opening the destination with no human reading it
A code photographed and opened later somewhere else, or shared so a second person lands on it
Camera apps that pre-fetch a destination before the person decides to open it
Scans driven by an incentive on the surface - a prize draw, a discount, a warranty registration - rather than by product interest
